strengths: Novel framework combining generative modeling with time-lagged conditional distributions for CV learning, well-motivated and clearly presented

Comprehensive evaluation across two different enhanced sampling techniques (SMD and OPES) with multiple complementary metrics (RMSD, THP, transition state energy, FES, φ distribution, free energy convergence)
Strong empirical results demonstrating superior transition state energies (33.58 vs 755-904 for baselines) and physically realistic transition paths through low-energy barriers
Excellent reproducibility with extensive experimental details, ablation studies validating design choices, and implementations of all baselines
Technically sound use of continuous normalizing flows, flow matching, and E(3)-equivariant networks with clear mathematical formulation
Good sensitivity analysis showing correlation with relevant atoms (dihedral angle related atoms) and clear visualization of results
weaknesses: Severely limited evaluation scope: only tested on Alanine Dipeptide (22 atoms, well-studied toy system) with 1D CVs; no evaluation on larger proteins or multi-dimensional CV problems, raising serious questions about generalizability
Computational cost analysis completely absent: no wall-clock time comparisons despite generative model training being more expensive than baselines; important for practical adoption

RMSD-aligned coordinate invariance is ad-hoc and problematic: CVs depend on reference state alignment rather than true SE(3) invariance; ablation shows heavy atom distances fail dramatically, suggesting performance may come from input representation rather than method

Significant inconsistencies in ablation results not adequately explained: removing autocorrelation loss improves THP to 97.27% but increases max energy to 116.58, raising questions about objective function alignment and which variant is actually superior

Lack of theoretical justification: no rigorous analysis of why conditioning generative models on encoders should capture slow dynamics; connection between p(x_t+τ|s_t) and slow manifold learning could be formalized
Hyperparameter sensitivity unexplored: autocorrelation loss weight λ and time lag τ=1000 fs not justified; no sensitivity analysis despite these being important design choices
Unexplained phenomenon: FES plots (Figure 5) show three metastable basins for TAE/TLC vs two for reference; unclear if these are physical or artifacts and whether this affects validity
Fairness of comparison concerns: DeepLDA/DeepTDA are supervised while TLC is unsupervised; different input representations (heavy atom distances vs RMSD coordinates) may confound results
No multi-dimensional CV evaluation despite real applications requiring 2+ CVs; scope of applicability uncertain
Missing practical details: training times, convergence criteria, hyperparameter selection procedures not documented
